metric.name: heap_growth_objects_by_class
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.memory.heap_graph.heap_graph_class_aggregation;
SELECT sum(value) AS value FROM (
SELECT type_name AS key, SUM(reachable_obj_count) AS value
FROM android_heap_graph_class_aggregation
WHERE graph_sample_ts = (
  SELECT MAX(graph_sample_ts) FROM android_heap_graph_class_aggregation
)
GROUP BY type_name
HAVING value > 0
ORDER BY key

)

claims.text: The available heap-object metric decreased from 399535 objects in the baseline to 399352 in the current trace, a delta of -183; this is not a regression in the measured metric.

claims.text: The observed class-level changes are small and are dominated by generic heap classes: float[] decreased from 641 to 534 and WeakHashMap$Entry from 275 to 201, while Object[] increased by 1, ArrayList by 1, and Long[] by 1.

citations.sql:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.memory.heap_graph.heap_graph_class_aggregation;
SELECT type_name, SUM(reachable_obj_count) AS reachable_objects
FROM android_heap_graph_class_aggregation
WHERE graph_sample_ts = (SELECT MAX(graph_sample_ts) FROM android_heap_graph_class_aggregation)
  AND type_name IN ('java.util.WeakHashMap$Entry', 'float[]', 'java.lang.Long[]', 'java.lang.Object[]', 'java.util.ArrayList')
GROUP BY type_name
ORDER BY type_name

caveats: the current trace's build was debuggable (run metadata: debuggable), so ART ran it with fewer optimisations and its timings overstate a release build's
Only one capture per side is available, so the -183-object difference may be run-to-run variation.
The frame, startup, binder, GC, scheduler, and native-heap metrics had no usable data in these traces; this conclusion is limited to the heap-object metric.
